theater: 肯特郡坎特伯雷與謝佩島

battle.name: 維京人第二次入侵不列顛群島
battle.theater: 肯特郡坎特伯雷與謝佩島
battle.brief: 980年北歐戰團再度登陸英國，自謝佩島直取坎特伯雷，掠走主教座堂的教會財貨；大主教鄧斯坦集結艦隊，在「艾塞爾港」毀其戰船，北軍載貨退回海上。這是「大異教軍」散去後第二波入侵的開場：登陸即掠、載貨而返。卡面科林斯青銅盔早於此一千六百年，「戴盔者只能靠隊形活」的道理在此換副面孔回來——靠盾牆上岸，靠艦隊封路。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries:
980年踏上英國土地的北歐戰團，在英格蘭編年史裡一律被記作「丹麥人」，實際是丹麥與挪威兩地的船隊聯合體。它不是國家常備軍：每支戰團由一位王或一位大領主率領，分成若干船隊作戰單位，首領在戰前會議決定打與不打，也決定戰利品如何分配；船上載人、馬匹、武器、口糧與貨幣工具，數日之間便可由一個海灣轉到另一個海灣。980年的進攻由丹麥王系與挪威王系共同推動：丹麥王斯韋恩・叉角（斯韋恩・福克比爾）在十世紀末整合丹麥王權，挪威王埃里克・布拉德阿克思於九八五年登上挪威王位，兩人都把英格蘭視為可以榨取財富的目標。北歐人在英國一帶另有據點：愛爾蘭的都柏林王國控制著愛爾蘭海航路，約克一帶的北歐聚落與北諾斯王國相連，這些落腳點使遠征有補給、有退路。
英格蘭一方是威塞克斯王國在九八〇年的實際狀態。國王埃塞爾雷德二世於父王埃德加於九七九年去世後即位，年僅十歲上下，政務由母后埃爾芙思里絲與一批重臣共同處理，核心是溫徹斯特的埃塞爾溫尼、索普科特郡的西格瓦德等人；英格蘭沒有常備軍，戰時依賴各郡的郡民徵召與各大戶的家臣團。約克的北歐君長與都柏林的諾斯人在這次戰役中的具體角色，英格蘭方面的記載幾乎空白，只能確定北歐人把英格蘭教會的財富當作可以定期提取的目標。教會一方並非旁觀者：坎特伯雷大主教鄧斯坦既是英格蘭教會領袖，也是軍事的策動者，編年史記他親自集結艦隊追擊北歐戰船，可見當時教會並未與戰爭脫節。
英格蘭的行政與金融中心集中在坎特伯雷——那座城市同時是阿爾弗雷德系諸王的舊都、主教座堂所在地與鑄幣場；北歐戰團在九八〇年的目標選擇，說明對方很清楚英格蘭的權力中樞與財富存放處究竟在哪裡。
countriesEn: The war band that set foot on English soil in 980 is called 'Danes' throughout the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, and in fact it was a coalition of fleets drawn from Denmark and Norway. It was not a standing national army: each war band was led by a king or a great magnate and split into ship companies as tactical units, and it was a council of these leaders that decided whether to fight at all and how the spoil was to be divided. The ships carried men, horses, weapons, rations and the tools of trade, and could move from one bay to another in the space of days. The offensive of 980 was pushed forward by the Danish and the Norwegian royal lines together: Sweyn Forkbeard consolidated the Danish kingship in the late tenth century, and Erik Bloodaxe took the Norwegian throne in 985, and both counted England as a source of wealth to be skimmed. The Northmen already held footholds in and around Britain: the Norse kingdom of Dublin in Ireland commanded the shipping of the Irish Sea, and the Scandinavian settlements around York were tied to the North Norwegian realm, and these gave the expedition supply and a line of retreat. On the English side stood the Kingdom of Wessex as it actually stood in 980. Æthelred II succeeded his father Edgar after Edgar's death in 979, at about ten years of age, and government was conducted by his mother Ælfthryth together with a group of senior nobles, at the centre of whom were Æthelwine of Winchester and Sigeweard of Exeter; England had no standing army and relied in wartime on the muster of each shire and on the households of the great landowners. The English record says almost nothing about the role of the Norse rulers of York or of the Norsemen of Dublin in this campaign, and all that can be established is that the Northmen treated the wealth of the English Church as a regular thing to be collected. The Church was not a bystander: Dunstan, Archbishop of Canterbury, was at once the head of the English Church and the organiser of the military response, the Chronicle recording that he himself gathered a fleet and went out against the Viking ships, which shows that the Church was not detached from the war. The administrative and financial centre of England was concentrated at Canterbury, a city that was at once the old capital of the Alfredian kings, the seat of the cathedral and the place of the mint; the target chosen by the war band in 980 shows that the other side knew very well where the power and the treasure of England were kept.
people:
留下姓名的關鍵人物，兩邊加起來不足十個，這本身就說明這場戰爭在文獻裡有多稀薄。
英格蘭方面，核心是坎特伯雷大主教鄧斯坦。他自九五九年出任坎特伯雷大主教，直到九八八年去世，是九八〇年那場戰役中唯一留下行動記錄的英格蘭統帥：編年史記他率艦隊赴「艾塞爾港」攻擊北歐戰船，毀其一部，迫使北軍放棄部分戰利品退回海上。鄧斯坦並非單純的教士形象，他出身卑微，早年在阿爾弗雷德宮廷中即以嚴格的苦行與自律聞名，後來主持英格蘭教會的本尼迪克特改革，要求修院有紀律、有戒律、有產出；這套教會組織力在三十年後成為英格蘭抵抗丹麥統治、維持地方秩序的骨架之一。年僅十歲的埃塞爾雷德二世在九八〇年尚未能親自指揮任何一場戰鬥，政權靠母后埃爾芙思里絲與重臣撐住；實際主持應對的是溫徹斯特的埃塞爾溫尼，他以精於軍事與地緣著稱，是英格蘭西、南部防線的支柱；索普科特郡的西格瓦德與埃塞爾瓦爾德等元老，同樣在這個階段的軍政中居於樞紐位置。
北歐方面，980年的入侵者多數沒有留下名字，編年史只寫「丹麥人」。但推動戰爭的君主是清楚的：挪威王埃里克・布拉德阿克思在九八五年即位後仍覬覦英格蘭北部，他先前在九四七至九五四年間兩度執掌約克，最後被英王埃德雷德逐出北境；丹麥王斯韋恩・叉角在九八六年前後接掌丹麥，把目標從劫掠轉為征服，他與挪威王室有姻親關係，兩家的行動互相支援。真正被英格蘭人記住姓名的北歐人是後來的奧拉夫・特里格瓦松，他與斯韋恩在九九四年聯手進攻倫敦，那是九八〇年之後北歐人最接近攻下英格蘭首都的一次。
戰役的另一端還有教會本身：坎特伯雷座堂的寶藏、聖物與現金被劫走，主教座堂的守備、逃難的教士與隨軍的抄經士，構成了另一種參與者；編年史裡「教會所屬的財貨」與「世俗的財貨」被分開記錄，正說明這場戰爭的戰利品是有分類的，而不是單純的破壞。
peopleEn: The named individuals on both sides together number fewer than ten, which in itself shows how thin the documentary record of this war is. On the English side the central figure is Dunstan, Archbishop of Canterbury. He held the see from 959 until his death in 988, and he is the only English commander of the campaign of 980 whose actions are actually recorded: the Chronicle has him take a fleet out to Ethel's port to attack the Viking ships, destroying a part of them and forcing the northern force to abandon part of its plunder and return to the sea. Dunstan was not a cleric in name only. He was of humble birth and was already known for strict asceticism and discipline in the court of Alfred, and he later drove the Benedictine reform of the English Church, requiring the monasteries to keep rule and order and to produce something; that organisational capacity of the Church was to become one of the skeletons of English resistance and local order thirty years later. Æthelred II, ten years old, was in 980 not yet able to command any action in person, and the government rested with his mother Ælfthryth and with the great nobles. The man who in practice directed the response was Æthelwine of Winchester, known for his skill in war and in geography and the mainstay of the western and southern defences of England; Sigeweard of Exeter and Æthelwald were of the same weight in the military government of these years. On the Norse side the invaders of 980 left no names, the Chronicle saying only 'the Danes'. The monarchs who drove the war are nevertheless clear: Erik Bloodaxe, on the Norwegian throne from 985, still coveted northern England, having held York twice between 947 and 954 before being driven out of the north by King Eadred; and Sweyn Forkbeard, who took over Denmark around 986 and shifted the aim from plunder to conquest, being related by marriage to the Norwegian royal house and supported by it. The Northman whose name the English did remember was Olaf Tryggvason, who joined Sweyn in the attack on London in 994, the closest the Northmen came to taking the English capital in the years after 980. On the other side of the fighting stands the Church itself: the treasure, the relics and the cash of Canterbury Cathedral were carried off, and the garrison of the cathedral, the clergy who fled and the scribes who marched with them formed another kind of participant. That the Chronicle records 'the treasure that belonged to the church of God' separately from 'the secular treasure' shows that the spoil of this war was classified, and that what was being done was not simple destruction.
kits:
先把最容易被誤讀的事講清楚：卡面上的科林斯青銅盔（Corinthian helmet）並沒有出現在980年的英格蘭。科林斯盔是公元前七世紀希臘城邦的產物，整體鍛造的青銅面甲只留出窄長的眼縫與鼻樑，奧林匹亞出土的樣本最為完整；到公元980年，這種全封閉的頭盔早已絕跡一千六百年有奇，希臘本土早已改用開口式的希臘式與伊利里亞式頭盔，北歐人更不可能擁有，北歐人在十世紀末戴的是鐵製鼻護盔與尖頂盔，重要場合才穿鏈甲盔。
但把這張卡放進這場戰爭並非毫無道理。科林斯盔最耐用的那一部分，是它揭示的交換條件：全正面開眼意味著戴盔者幾乎看不見兩側，聽覺與視野都要打折，行動上必然依附身旁的同伴——「戴它的人只能靠隊形活」。這正是980年肯特郡登陸戰的寫照：北歐戰團靠的不是個人技藝，而是船隊登岸後立刻結成的盾牆；英格蘭方面同樣沒有可以倚賴的個人武藝，靠的是郡民徵召來的步兵、家臣團的劍盾，以及大主教組織起來的艦隊。盾牆與科林斯盔背後是同一個原理：把個人藏進隊形之中，讓正面變成一道沒有弱點的牆；北軍靠它登岸與護住戰利品，英格蘭人靠艦隊封住退路，兩邊都是用隊形代替個人。
北歐戰團實際的裝備以雙刃直劍、闊刃長柄斧與長矛為主，配圓盾與較晚出現的翼形長盾，鎧甲是歐洲當時最紮實的一批：鎖子甲上衣配皮革襯裡；弓只是輔助，主要搏鬥發生在盾牆與斧、劍之間。英格蘭方面，肯特郡的家臣團與後來倫敦的市民武裝裝備與北歐大同小異，鎖子甲同樣稀有，主流是皮甲、木盾與矛；直到九八〇年代之後，靠丹麥金維持的家臣團才普遍穿鎖子甲。攻城方面，980年北軍在坎特伯雷以火與撞擊對付城門與城牆，沒有留下可考的攻城塔；英格蘭的城防靠牆垣與城樓，防守靠守軍而非攻城器。運輸與補給全部靠船：淺吃水的長船供戰士划槍作戰，寬腹的貨船載運戰利品、馬匹與糧食；編年史不記船數，通行說法只說「大軍」。值得注意的是980年這支船隊不像九二〇年攻愛爾蘭那樣攜帶大量馬匹，行動是純粹的海陸閃擊，戰利品直接從主教座堂裝船運走。
kitsEn: First the thing most easily misread must be said plainly: the Corinthian helmet on the card did not appear in England in 980. The Corinthian helmet was a product of the Greek city states of the seventh century BC, a bronze face-piece hammered as a unit with only a narrow eye slot and a nasal left open, of which the example found at Olympia is the most complete; by AD 980 that fully closed helmet had been extinct for something like sixteen hundred years, the Greek mainland had long since adopted open-faced Greek and Illyrian types, and the Northmen could certainly not have had one: what they wore in the late tenth century was the iron nasal helm and the conical spangenhelm, with a mail helm reserved for occasions of importance. Yet the card is not idle in this war. The durable part of the Corinthian helmet is the terms it reveals: an eye slit across the whole face means the wearer can scarcely see to either side, hearing and vision are both diminished, and his action must lean on the man next to him, so that he can only live inside the formation. That is the picture of the landing in Kent in 980. The Viking war band rested on no individual skill but on the wall of shields formed the moment the crews came ashore; and the English had no individual prowess to lean on either, but the foot brought in by the shire muster, the swords and shields of the household retainers, and above all the fleet organised by the archbishop. The shield wall and the Corinthian helmet rest on the same principle: the individual is folded into the formation so that the front becomes a wall without a weak point. The northern side used it to land and to cover the plunder; the English used the fleet to seal the way back; on both sides it was the formation that stood in place of the individual. As for the actual equipment of the war band: double-edged straight swords, broad-bladed long-handled axes and spears, with round shields and, later, kite-shaped shields, and armour among the best in contemporary Europe, a mail shirt worn over a leather lining; the bow was a secondary arm, for the real work was done between the wall of shields and the axe and sword. On the English side the household retainers of Kent, and later the civic levy of London, were equipped much the same way, mail still rare, the norm being leather armour, wooden shields and spears; it was only after the 980s, with the Danegeld paying for them, that the housecarls were generally found in mail. On siege work, the northern force at Canterbury used fire and impact against gates and curtain walls, and no identifiable siege tower survives; the English defences rested on wall and tower, and on the garrison rather than on engines. Transport and supply were entirely a matter of ships: shallow-draught longships for the warriors to row and fight from, and broad-bellied cargo ships for the plunder, the horses and the grain. The annals give no number of ships, and the usual phrase is only of a great host. It is worth noting that the fleet of 980 did not, like the one that attacked Ireland in 920, carry a great number of horses: the operation was a pure sea-to-land raid, and the loot went straight from the cathedral into the holds.
tactics:
980年這場戰役的打法，可以分成北歐與英格蘭兩串動作來看。
北歐一方的第一招是選港。編年史記北軍先在肯特北岸的「艾塞爾港」集結，那地方通常被認為在旺特瑟姆海峽一帶，該海峽在十世紀仍能通航，是把船駛入內陸、避開外海敵艦的門戶；海峽內的潮流決定了登岸時機，長船吃水淺，可以趁高潮越過灘地、直接靠上陸地。第二招是搶時間內陸行軍：從港口到坎特伯雷不過二十餘公里，車馬一天之內可達，主力一登岸便直取教區，目標不是佔領郡治，而是主教座堂與城內的教會財貨。第三招是快速裝載：教會的器皿、聖物、祭衣、現金與世俗財貨只要能搬上船就是戰利品，難以搬走的一概留在原地，說明這支軍隊沒有長期駐紮的打算。第四招是結盾牆行軍與自保：登岸隊伍與船隊之間必須保持可守的距離，隊形一散，掠得的東西就變成別人的戰利品。第五招是撤退有路：全軍帶著戰利品退回船隊所在的港灣，再循海峽出海，整個行動的時間以數週計。
英格蘭一方的動作同樣清楚。坎特伯雷大主教鄧斯坦在北軍劫掠之後迅速在「艾塞爾港」集結艦隊，趕在北軍重新登船之前攻擊其戰船，毀掉一部分，使北軍無法把全部掠得物帶走，殘部只能分散登船逃出；英格蘭沒有能力追擊到海上追殲，只能以封鎖港口的方式切斷退路。英格蘭這邊還有第二層教訓：郡民徵召來的步兵與家臣團可以作戰，但集合緩慢、裝備不一，編年史記「肯特軍與大主教會合」正說明這是一支拼湊起來、人數有限的部隊，遇上的是一支編制完整、裝備統一的登岸戰團。
這一整套打法與八六五至八七八年「大異教軍」那一次不同：那一次北歐人是登陸建國、分地而治；九八〇年這一次是登陸即掠、載貨而返，不打算留下。這也解釋了為何英格蘭的記載只寫財貨被劫而不寫城市被攻陷：城牆被破不等於佔領，破了就走，才是這一波入侵的邏輯。
tacticsEn: The way this campaign of 980 was fought can be read as two sequences of moves, one on each side. The first move of the Northmen was the choice of a harbour. The Chronicle has the host assembling at Ethel's port on the north coast of Kent, a place generally taken to be in the region of the Wantsum Channel, which was still navigable in the tenth century and served as the doorway by which ships could slip inside the coast and out of reach of enemy squadrons; the tides inside the channel set the timing of the landing, and because longships are shallow of draught they could cross the flats and take the ground directly at high water. The second move was the forced march inland. From the harbour to Canterbury is no more than twenty-odd kilometres, a day's march for horse and cart, and the main body went straight for the episcopal city the moment it was ashore: the aim was not to take the county town but the cathedral and the church treasure within it. The third move was fast loading. Vessels, relics, vestments, cash and secular valuables that could be carried were the prize, and whatever could not be carried was left where it lay, which shows that this force had no intention of staying. The fourth was the discipline of the shield wall on the march and of the baggage guard: the distance between the landed column and the ships had to be defensible, because once the formation broke, the plunder became somebody else's plunder. The fifth was the line of retreat: the whole force took its loot back to the harbour where the fleet lay and stood out to sea by the channel, and the whole operation was measured in weeks rather than seasons. The English moves are equally plain. As soon as the raiding was done, Dunstan of Canterbury gathered a fleet at Ethel's port and struck the Viking ships before the northern force could re-embark, destroying a part of them; the survivors could only scatter into boats and get away. The English could not pursue to sea and annihilate, so they cut the way off at the harbour instead. There was a second lesson for the English as well: the foot brought in by the shire muster and the household retainers could fight, but mustering was slow and equipment was uneven, and the phrase in the Chronicle that 'the Kentish host and the archbishop' met the Danes says plainly that this was a patched-together force of limited numbers facing a landing war band that was uniform in organisation and equipment. The whole method differs from that of the Great Heathen Army of 865 to 878. That army landed and founded, divided the land and ruled it; the force of 980 landed, plundered, loaded and left, with no intention of remaining. That is why the English record speaks of treasure being taken rather than of a city being occupied: breaking the wall was not the same as settling, and break and go was the logic of this second wave.
data:
可核對的數字分三類，而這場戰爭最硬的一條時間線是編年史本身。
第一類是《英格蘭編年史》關於九八〇年的記載：北軍在「艾塞爾港」登陸，進攻坎特伯雷，肯特軍與大主教會合應戰，「教會所屬的財貨」與「世俗的財貨」皆被掠去；其後大主教集結艦隊，在港口毀其戰船一部，北軍殘部逃回海上。必須說明的是，同一段記載在不同的抄本與不同年代的編訂本中分別被繫於九八〇年與九九一年，這說明編年史家自己也未確定年份；同一批事件的另一種安排是繫於九八八年，該年肯特在謝佩島擊敗北軍，英軍隨後渡海燒毀丹麥沿岸一座市鎮，地名有異說。編年史只標年份不標月份，把這一輪出擊放在航海季中——北歐船隊的行動必須在夏季可航的月份完成，是通行做法。
第二類是編年史與文物互證的數字。全英出土的十世紀錢窖以倫敦為最著，1990年代在倫敦出土的一批約含八萬七千枚銀便士，年代屬九九四年前後，是英格蘭鑄幣史上規模最大的單批發現，說明北歐戰爭直接衝擊的是英格蘭的貨幣經濟。至於丹麥金，一〇一六年為止的累積支付被編年史記為四萬八千磅白銀，這筆錢正是英格蘭此後二十年在軍事上依賴外來僱兵的財政基礎。英格蘭約克郡與東英格蘭的大區域由丹麥法權統治，約佔英格蘭的三分之一；英格蘭全境人口在十世紀末的估計多在百萬上下，分歧頗大。
第三類是必須打折扣的推估。編年史不記北軍的船數與兵數，只寫「大軍」；980年這支船隊的規模，通行推測為數十艘長船，遠小於八六五年的「大異教軍」。雙方的戰鬥傷亡完全沒有可靠記載，任何精確數字都屬後人推想，不應引用。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes, and the hardest timeline this war possesses is the Chronicle itself. The first is the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle's entry for 980: the host landed at Ethel's port, struck at Canterbury, the Kentish host and the archbishop met them, and 'the treasure that belonged to the church of God' and the secular treasure were both carried off; afterwards the archbishop gathered a fleet at the harbour and destroyed a part of the Viking ships, and the remnant got back to the sea. It must be said that the same passage is attached to 980 in some manuscripts and editions and to 991 in others, which means the annalists were not themselves certain of the year; another arrangement of the same events attaches them to 988, the year in which Kent beat the northern force on the Isle of Sheppey and the English fleet then crossed to Denmark and burned a town on the Danish coast, whose name is variously given. The Chronicle marks the year and not the month; the practice of placing such an operation in the middle of the sailing season, since a northern fleet could only move in the months the sea allowed, is the received one. The second class is the numbers that the Chronicle and the archaeology confirm between them. The largest tenth-century coin hoards in England come from London, and a group found in the 1990s in the City contained some eighty-seven thousand silver pennies, dated to around 994, the largest single find in the history of English coinage and direct evidence of what the Viking wars did to the English monetary economy. As for the Danegeld, the Chronicle records the accumulated payments up to 1016 as forty-eight thousand pounds of silver, and that money was the financial basis on which England depended for foreign mercenaries for the twenty years that followed. A third of England, the great districts of Yorkshire and East Anglia, lay under Danish law, and the population of England as a whole at the end of the tenth century is commonly put in the region of a million, with wide disagreement between estimates. The third class is estimate, and has to be discounted. The Chronicle gives neither the number of ships nor the number of men in the northern host, saying only of a great host; the fleet of 980 is usually guessed at several tens of longships, far smaller than the Great Heathen Army of 865. As for the losses of the fighting, no reliable figure survives at all, and any exact number is later speculation that should not be quoted.
cause:
打起來有四層原因，一層推一層。
最外一層是結構性的變化：八六五至八七八年的「大異教軍」散夥之後，北歐人的遠征形式變了。不再是一整支大軍登陸建國、分地而治，而是由丹麥與挪威的王權直接推動、以劫掠與勒索為目的的定期打擊；九八〇年正是這種新形式的開場，參戰者第一次不是自由的戰團，而是受王命行動的船隊。第二層是英格蘭教會的財富結構。坎特伯雷主教座堂是九八〇年歐洲最富的教會財富之一：聖物、金器、祭衣與現金高度集中，卻沒有足以長期抵抗登岸戰團的守備，財物又笨重不便遠運——這種目標對遠征者而言是「取之即走」的理想目標，而九八〇年的編年史恰恰說明對方是這樣算帳的。第三層是英格蘭的軍政弱點。埃塞爾雷德二世即位時只有十歲，國政由母后與重臣共同處理，沒有常備軍，沒有海軍，郡民徵召的召集與裝備都需時間；英格蘭在南岸與倫敦方向唯一成形的自衛力量是倫敦市民的武裝，而那要到九九六年才正式建立。第四層是航海技術的成熟：十世紀的北歐造船已能用搭接式船殼造出吃水淺、可上帆亦可用槳、又能在灘地擺脫的長船，使遠征者能從海灣直入內陸水道，而英格蘭沒有對等的船隊，唯一的海上反擊手段是教會與貴族臨時湊起來的艦隊。
地緣與利益把這四層扣在一起：旺特瑟姆海峽是進入肯特內陸的捷徑，坎特伯雷是英格蘭權力與財富的匯聚點；北歐人算準了英格蘭的弱點在哪裡，便年年可以來取。
causeEn: There are four layers of cause, each resting on the one below it. The outermost is a structural change: after the Great Heathen Army broke up between 865 and 878, the form of the Norse expedition changed. There was no longer a single great army landing to found a kingdom and divide the land, but repeated strikes aimed at plunder and blackmail, driven directly by the royal power of Denmark and Norway; 980 is the opening of that new form, and for the first time the participants were not free war bands but fleets acting by royal command. The second layer is the wealth structure of the English Church. The cathedral at Canterbury was among the richest concentrations of church treasure in Europe in 980: relics, gold plate, vestments and cash gathered in one place, defended by no force capable of holding out against a landing war band, and too heavy to carry far. For an expedition, that made it the ideal target, one to be taken and left again, and the Chronicle's entry for 980 shows the other side doing exactly that kind of arithmetic. The third layer is the military and political weakness of England. Æthelred II came to the throne at ten years of age, government was conducted by his mother and a council of great nobles, there was no standing army and no navy, and the mustering and equipping of the shire levies took time; the only self-defence force that actually took shape in the south and at London was the civic levy of the Londoners, and that was not established until 996. The fourth layer is the maturity of the seamanship: tenth-century Norse hulls, built with clinker planking, could be made shallow enough of draught to sail as well as row, and to be floated off a beach, which let the raider move from the bay into the inland waterways, and England had no fleet to match it, the only counter-force afloat being such fleets as the Church and the great households could raise in haste. Geography and interest then locked the four layers together: the Wantsum Channel was the short road into the interior of Kent, Canterbury was where the power and the treasure of England met, and the Northmen had calculated exactly where the weakness lay, so that they could come year after year to collect.
impact:
這場戰爭留下的東西，比它的勝負更持久。
第一，暴露英格蘭海岸的空門。九八〇年的教會財貨被劫，證明只要有船隊能進入旺特瑟姆海峽，兩天之內就可以把英格蘭最重要的一座城市的財富搬空；此後英格蘭的沿海防衛體系被徹底重整：九八〇年代末期開始興建所謂「堡壘」（burh），把海港與要衝築成可屯兵的自衛點，最終形成環繞英格蘭海岸的堡壘網絡；倫敦在九九六年正式組織市民武裝，是英格蘭最早的城市自衛制度；英格蘭王室的艦隊亦在這一時期開始被視為國策。這三件事的共同背景，都是九八〇年之後年年再來的北歐登陸。
第二，帶來了丹麥金與英格蘭軍制的轉向。北歐人以劫掠為常態，英格蘭以錢贖命，逐步把國防支出從徵召農兵的郡民體系轉向以金錢維持的職業家臣團；這支由丹麥金養活的職業軍隊在九八〇年代之後成型，一〇一六年為止累積支付四萬八千磅白銀，成為英格蘭在九八〇年之後的戰爭主力，也讓北歐人自己也看見「以金制敵」的辦法確實可行，遂在一〇一三年至一〇一四年間直接把征服的軍隊渡過北海。
第三，錢幣與考古層把戰爭的代價留在了地下。倫敦出土的近九萬枚便士錢窖顯示這場戰爭對英格蘭貨幣流通的衝擊，肯特郡沿海一帶十世紀的聚落層、兵器與船塢遺址則顯示北歐船隊活動的範圍遠不限於一次襲擊。
第四，敘事的重塑。九八〇年前後的襲擊讓英格蘭編年史進入「年年記錄北歐來犯」的常態，維京人不再是偶發的盜匪，而是一個有國王、有計畫、有下一次的政治力量；英格蘭人從此對「海上有另一個帝國」保持警覺，這種警覺延續到一〇一六年克努特即位後的北方帝國時代。
impactEn: What this war left behind is more durable than its outcome. First, it exposed the open door on the English coast. The church treasure taken in 980 proved that once a fleet could enter the Wantsum Channel, the wealth of the most important city in England could be carried off within two days. The coastal defence system of England was therefore rebuilt from the ground: the burhs, the fortified places, were begun in the late 980s, turning harbours and strategic points into self-supporting garrisons, and in the end they formed a ring of fortifications around the English coast; the civic levy of London was formally organised in 996, the earliest urban self-defence institution in England; and a royal fleet came to be treated as a matter of policy. All three grew out of the northern landings that followed 980 year by year. Second came the Danegeld and the turn in the English way of war. With raiding becoming the northern habit, and with England buying off its attacks with money, national defence spending moved away from the shire levy of part-time farmers and towards professional households paid in cash; that force, the housecarls maintained by the Danegeld, took shape in the 980s and was the English war-making instrument for the following decades, and the 48,000 pounds of silver paid away by 1016 showed the Northmen that buying off an enemy worked, which is why in 1013 and 1014 they simply brought the army of conquest across the sea instead. Third, the cost of the war is preserved underground in coin and in the soil: a London hoard of nearly ninety thousand pennies bears witness to the shock the wars dealt to English circulation, while the tenth-century levels of the settlement, weapons and boatyard remains along the Kentish coast show that the activity of the northern fleets was far wider than a single raid. Fourth, the narrative was remade. The raids around 980 put the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle into a permanent register of 'the Northmen come again this year'; the Viking was no longer an occasional bandit but a political power with kings, plans and a next time, and the English became permanently alert to the fact that there was another empire across the sea, an alertness that ran on into the age of the North Sea empire under Cnut after 1016.
result:
就980年這一段而言，結果是清楚的：丹麥人贏了錢，英格蘭人贏了港口。
北軍在肯特郡得手，掠走坎特伯雷主教座堂的教會財貨與世俗財貨，隨後被鄧斯坦在「艾塞爾港」集結的艦隊截住，一部戰船被毀，殘餘戰利品未能盡數帶走，北軍只能分散登船、循海峽退走。對英格蘭來說這是一場典型的「守住國土卻失掉財富」的失敗：城牆被破不等於國土淪陷，但主教座堂的損失要靠幾代人的捐獻才能補回，日後坎特伯雷的重建工程正是在填補這個洞。對北歐人來說則是一次成功的、有利可圖的襲擊——正是這種能年年重演、卻不必駐紮的戰法，後來被反覆使用。
但整場「第二次入侵」遠未在980年結束。988年肯特在謝佩島擊敗北軍並把艦隊送到丹麥海岸，九九一年莫爾登的戰鬥與隨後第一筆丹麥金，九九四年兩王聯手進攻倫敦，九九七年以後北歐戰團深入威塞克斯腹地，最終在一〇一三年至一〇一四年由斯韋恩・叉角完成對英格蘭的征服，一〇一六年克努特登基後，英格蘭成為一個北海帝國的一部分。從980年算起，英格蘭用二十六年時間把一次襲擊的教訓變成了一整套制度——倫敦的市民武裝、堡壘網絡、以金養兵的家臣團——而這些制度恰恰在征服到來時顯示出局限。
卡面科林斯青銅盔的原理也在這裡走完一條長弧：它在公元前七世紀的希臘是一頂真正的工藝品，而在980年的肯特，它只剩下「戴盔者只能靠隊形活」這條道理——北軍靠盾牆登岸、靠隊形護住戰利品，英格蘭人靠艦隊與郡民結成的整體擋住退路。第二波維京入侵的勝負從來不是由哪一個武藝超群的個人決定的，而由誰能把更多人變成一面完整的牆決定。
resultEn: As for the campaign of 980 itself, the result is plain: the Danes won the money and the English won the harbour. The northern force got into Kent and carried off the church treasure and the secular treasure of Canterbury Cathedral, and was then cut off at Ethel's port by the fleet Dunstan had gathered, a part of their ships was destroyed, part of the plunder could not be carried away, and the survivors scattered into boats and withdrew by the channel. For England this was a defeat of the familiar kind: the country was held, but the wealth was lost. Breaking a wall was not the loss of the country, but the damage to the cathedral could only be made good by the gifts of generations, and the rebuilding works at Canterbury in later centuries were filling precisely that gap. For the Northmen it was a successful and profitable raid, and it was this repeatable form of warfare, harried and never settled, that was used again and again. But the whole second invasion did not end in 980. Kent beat the northern force on the Isle of Sheppey in 988 and sent its fleet to the Danish coast; there was the fight at Maldon in 991 and the first Danegeld; the two kings struck at London together in 994; from 997 the northern war bands went deep into Wessex; and finally Sweyn Forkbeard completed the conquest of England in 1013 and 1014, with Cnut on the throne in 1016 and England part of a North Sea empire. Counting from 980, England took twenty-six years to turn the lesson of a raid into a whole set of institutions, a civic levy in London, a ring of burhs, and households of professional soldiers kept on cash, and those institutions were exactly the ones that showed their limits when the conquest came. The principle of the Corinthian helmet on the card also runs a long arc here. In the Greek world of the seventh century BC it was a real piece of craft; at Canterbury in 980 it retained only the single proposition that the man in the closed helm can only live inside the formation: the northern side landed behind a wall of shields and kept its plunder safe by standing in a formation, and the English, with their fleet and the shire levy drawn together, held the way back by acting as a whole. Nothing in the second Viking invasion was ever decided by a single outstanding warrior; it was decided by whoever could turn more men into one unbroken wall.
